verses.147:1: {v1open}, o Senhor: * louva o teu Deus, Sião.
verses.147:2: Porque fortaleceu {seras} das tuas portas: * {benedixit} os teus filhos {inte}.
verses.147:4: {q4} envia à terra {eloquium}: * depressa corre a sua palavra.
verses.147:5: {q5} dá a neve como lã: * espalha a névoa como cinza.
verses.147:6: Lança o seu {crystallum} {buccellas}: * {faciem} do seu frio, quem subsistirá?
verses.147:7: Enviará a sua palavra, e os derreterá: * soprará o seu {spiritus}, e {fluent} as águas.
verses.147:8: {q8} anuncia a sua palavra a Jacó: * {justitias} e os seus juízos a Israel.
verses.147:9: Não fez assim {omni}: * e não lhes manifestou os seus juízos.

decisions.why: Jerusalem is a single addressee, not God: tu (rule 3), as the Latin's singular 'Lauda'. The Latin has no 'O'. The build is 112:1's ('Louvai, meninos, o Senhor', no 'ó'), so the same here. Row 'vocative plural of persons' (28:1) supplies 'ó' where a vocative can be heard as the object; here 'o Senhor' follows at once and the comma is sung, so it is left out, keeping the two colons alike as in the Latin. The Brazilian lectionary/LH line is 'Glorifica o Senhor, Jerusalém … celebra teu Deus, ó Sião' (circulation.md): from the Hebrew's verb; the Latin's is laudáre → louvar.

options.label: Louva, Jerusalém
options.note: draft — as 112:1, no vocative particle, as the Latin

options.label: Louva, ó Jerusalém
options.note: MS1932; the 'ó' tells the vocative from the object (row of 28:1)

options.label: Glorifica, Jerusalém
options.note: the Brazilian lectionary's verb (circulation.md). Refused: glorificáre has its own word, and laudáre is louvar in every psalm

decisions.latin: Qui pósuit … Qui emíttit … Qui dat … Qui annúntiat
decisions.why: Four relative clauses hang from the God of 147:1 with no main verb (147:6–7 then go on with plain verbs, 'Mittit … Emíttet'). A bare 'Que pôs … Que envia … Que dá' at the head of a verse is heard as a question ('Que dá?') or a wish; MS1932 makes each a cleft ('É ele que'). The draft names the subject in a main clause, 'Ele …', four times, as 65:9 ('Ele pôs a minha alma para a vida') and 134:10 ('Ele feriu') did: the Latin's anaphora is kept as a repeated 'Ele', the relative is grammar (D2).

options.label: Ele pôs … Ele envia … Ele dá … Ele anuncia
É ele que pôs … É ele que envia …
options.note: MS1932 ('Foi ele que … É ele que'); two syllables longer in each colon

options.label: Que pôs … Que envia …
options.note: the Latin's relative; heard as a question at the head of a verse

decisions.why: Sera is the bar put across a door (L&S). 106:16 'vectes férreos' is 'as trancas de ferro', and the glossary row (vectis) notes that 147:2 is another word. The Greek has μοχλούς in both places, so D15's test would allow one word; but the Latin has two and 'ferrolhos' costs nothing: it is plain, MS1932's, and one blind reader did not know 'trancas' (106:16).

options.note: draft — MS1932 'os ferrolhos'; DRB 'the bolts'

options.label: as trancas
options.note: = 106:16 vectis (the same Greek μοχλός)

decisions.why: The Latin says only 'in you'. 'em ti' keeps it, and with it the reading 'in you = through you' that the Latin does not exclude. DRB 'within thee' and MS1932 '(que habitam) dentro de ti' make it place.

decisions.why: A double accusative: 'set your borders (as) peace' (Greek ὁ τιθεὶς τὰ ὅριά σου εἰρήνην, the same build). 43:14 'Posuísti nos oppróbrium' became 'Fizestes de nós uma afronta', but 'fez das tuas fronteiras a paz' is not a sentence anyone says. The draft moves the peace into the object and the borders into a place, as both Vulgate-family versions do (DRB 'hath placed peace in thy borders', MS1932 'estabeleceu a paz nas tuas fronteiras'): words and image kept, grammar changed (D2). This is the line of the Corpus Christi and Marian Vespers; the Brazilian LH/lectionary has 'A paz em teus limites garantiu' (circulation.md, Hebrew-based). 'fines' of a city's territory is 'fronteiras'; the glossary's 'confins' (7:7a, 'fines terræ' → 'os confins da terra') is heard in Brazil as the far ends of the earth, and 'os teus confins' as remote corners.

decisions.why: The same noun phrase as 80:17 'ex ádipe fruménti' → 'da gordura do trigo', so the same words (rule 6); the adeps row keeps the concrete fat (rule 5), and saturáre/satiáre → saciar. The Brazilian LH and lectionary say 'a flor do trigo' (circulation.md) — the Hebrew idiom's sense 'the finest', and MS1932's 'da flor da farinha'; kept as an option because it is the line Brazilians know from Corpus Christi, but it replaces the Latin's image with its meaning.

options.label: da gordura do trigo
options.note: draft — = 80:17; DRB 'the fat of corn'

options.label: da flor do trigo
options.note: the Brazilian LH/lectionary wording (fetched); MS1932 'da flor da farinha'. An interpretation of 'adeps'

decisions.latin: Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo ejus
decisions.why: One of the verses D15 and D26 left to decide locally: elóquium (λόγιον) and sermo (λόγος) side by side, and three verses on, verbum (λόγος again) twice → 'palavra'. D15's test keeps apart what the Greek keeps apart: sermo and verbum are one word (palavra), elóquium is another. Outside Ps 118 elóquium has gone to 'palavra' where it stood alone (11:7, 17:31, 104:19, 106:11); here that would give 'a sua palavra … a sua palavra' in one verse where the Latin varies. The draft uses D26's clause in the present, as 103:34 'o que digo': 'Ele envia à terra o que diz' — an object, so no genitive forces a noun. MS1932 'as suas ordens' interprets.

options.label: o que diz
options.note: draft — D26's clause, present as 103:34

options.label: a sua palavra (sermo → a sua fala)
options.note: as 11:7, 104:19; then the second colon would want 'fala' (55:11) to keep the Latin's variation — not filled here: this option alone repeats 'palavra' in the verse

options.label: o seu dito
options.note: the noun D16 tried; refused by the stylist nine times in Pss 11 and 118

options.label: gelo
options.note: draft — L&S sense 1; MS1932

options.label: cristal
options.note: DRB 'his crystal'; the Latin's word, heard as glass

decisions.why: The row 'ante fáciem → diante da face de' (open) keeps the Hebraism, as DRB 'before the face of his cold'. The face of the cold is odd in Portuguese as in Latin; it is the Latin's image. MS1932 'ao rigor do seu frio' explains it. The question ends as 129:3's formula 'quis sustinébit?' → 'quem subsistirá?'.

options.label: diante da face
options.note: draft — the row; DRB

options.label: ao rigor
options.note: MS1932; the image explained away

decisions.why: Spíritus (πνεῦμα) is wind and spirit at once; in the thaw it is the wind first, and DRB and MS1932 both say 'wind'. The row of 102:16 chose 'sopro' to keep both, but here the verb is 'flabit' and 'soprará o seu sopro' makes a figure the Latin does not have (the Greek does: πνεύσει τὸ πνεῦμα). The draft keeps the Latin's word, 'espírito', lower case as D44 (50:13) and 142:10b: the Latin leaves the Spirit audible and 'vento' would close it. The ambiguity reader should say whether the wind is still heard.

options.label: espírito
options.note: draft — the Latin's word, both senses open

options.label: vento
options.note: DRB 'his wind', MS1932 'o seu vento'; closes the ambiguity

options.label: sopro
options.note: the row of 102:16; with 'soprará' it doubles the root

decisions.why: The same words as 77:20 and 104:41 'et fluxérunt aquæ' → 'e correram as águas', so the same verb (rule 6). The row 'decúrrere / flúere → correr / escorrer' (57:8–9) split them only where both stand together; 96:5 has 'escorreram' of wax. Cost: 'correr' also renders 'currit' three verses up (147:4), a merger the Latin does not make.

options.label: escorrerão
options.note: the row's word for flúere (57:9); keeps it apart from currit in 147:4

decisions.why: The plural justítiæ row (10:8) is open with 'as justiças'. Here the Greek is δικαιώματα, which elsewhere the Latin renders 'justificatiónes' (→ 'preceitos', D15); but the Latin says justítias and is followed (rule 1). DRB 'his justices', MS1932 'as suas justiças'. 'sua' governs both nouns; Portuguese repeats the possessive.

options.label: as suas justiças
options.note: draft — DRB, MS1932

options.label: os seus preceitos
options.note: the Greek's word (δικαιώματα = justificatiónes); refused, not the Latin

decisions.why: 'Non … omni' is literally 'not to every nation', a Hebraism for 'to none (other)'. 'Não fez assim a todas as nações' keeps the Latin's form, and the Portuguese says what is meant: this was not done for all, only for Israel. 'a nenhuma outra nação' (DM1962 'a nenhum outro povo', from the Hebrew) resolves it and supplies 'outra'. The plural is grammar: 'a toda nação' is heard as 'to every nation' and blurs.

options.label: a todas as nações
options.note: draft — the Latin's form; MS1932 'a todas as outras nações' less 'outras'

options.label: a nenhuma outra nação
options.note: resolves the idiom and adds 'outra'

choices.147:1: No title: DO's Psalm147.txt begins at 'Lauda, Jerúsalem'; it has no 'Allelúja' line (the LXX has αλληλουια Αγγαιου καὶ Ζαχαριου; MS1932 prints 'Aleluia'). Nothing to translate under D7. 'Sião' as the glossary.
choices.147:2: Quóniam → Porque (default). confortáre → fortalecer, the verb of the confortári row. The second colon has no 'and', as the Latin.
choices.147:3: saturáre/satiáre → saciar (row). Word order of the second colon kept from the Latin (verb last), as 80:17.
choices.147:4: velóciter → depressa (row); the Latin's order kept, adverb first, so the colon ends on 'palavra' (sermo → palavra, D15).
choices.147:5: 'dá' for 'dat', the Latin's plain verb (MS1932 'faz cair' explains). nébula → névoa (ὁμίχλη, mist; the Hebrew's frost not followed).
choices.147:6: Mittit → Lança (βάλλοντος, throwing; as the míttere rows 21:18, 80:15) kept apart from emíttere → enviar (147:4, 147:7; row of 103:10). 'quem subsistirá?' = 129:3.
choices.147:7: 'Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea' is built as 106:20 'Misit verbum suum, et sanávit eos' → 'Enviou a sua palavra, e os curou'; so 'Enviará a sua palavra, e os derreterá'. 'ea' (neuter plural: the snow, mist and ice) → 'os'. liquefácere → derreter (row of 74:4). Soft flag: second colon +4 by the counter, which does not elide; sung, 'seu‿espírito' and 'e‿correrão' close it to about +2. Accepted: nothing can go without losing a word of the Latin.
choices.147:8: Jacob → Jacó; judícia → juízos (D15). Soft flag: first colon +4 by the counter; 'Ele‿anuncia‿a sua' elides to about +2. The named subject 'Ele' (decision qui) costs the rest.
choices.147:9: manifestáre → manifestar (row of 79:2b). The object moved after the verb (natural order, D2); the Latin puts 'judícia sua' first. Soft flag: second colon -3 (the Latin's long 'manifestávit'); accepted.

audit.note: v1 from the parallels (consult/parallels/ps147.md), glossary and concordance (ps147/concord.py). Brazilian circulation fetched (circulation.md): the lectionary/LH say 'Glorifica o Senhor, Jerusalém' and 'a flor do trigo', both Hebrew-based; neither taken. Hard readings: 147:3 the double accusative 'pósuit fines tuos pacem'; 147:4 elóquium beside sermo; 147:7 spíritus (wind/spirit); 147:9 'non … omni'. D7: no title line in DO's Latin, none added. Pss 145–146 are being drafted in parallel; neither folder had a prayed text when this was written.
hard pass (ids and marks). Soft: 147:7b +4, 147:8a +4, 147:9b -3 syllables by the heuristic counter, each accepted in choices; no rhyme or cadence flags.
